title.raw: 卷七十六 列傳第二十六: 太宗諸子 Volume 76 Biographies 26: Taizong's Sons

sentences.zh: =褚遂良=

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang

sentences.zh: 褚遂良，散騎常侍亮之子也。

translations.literal: Chu Suiliang was the son of Liang, Palace Attendant at Large.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Suiliang was the son of Chu Liang, who had served as Palace Attendant at Large.

sentences.zh: 太業末，隨父在隴右，薛舉僭號，署為通事舍人。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, he followed his father in Longyou; Xue Ju usurped the title and appointed him Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Daye reign, he accompanied his father to Longyou. When Xue Ju declared himself emperor, he appointed Chu as Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 舉敗歸國，授秦州都督府鎧曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Ju was defeated he returned to the state and was appointed Armor Records Officer in the Qinzhou Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: After Xue Ju was defeated, Chu returned to the Tang court and was appointed Records Officer for Armor in the Qinzhou Area Command headquarters.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十年，自秘書郎遷起居郎。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenguan, he was moved from Secretary to Attendant of the Imperial Diary.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhenguan, he was promoted from Secretary to Attendant who records the emperor's movements.

sentences.zh: 遂良博涉文史，尤工隸書，父友歐陽詢甚重之。

translations.literal: Suiliang was broadly versed in literature and history and especially skilled in clerical script; his father's friend Ouyang Xun greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang was widely read in literature and history and especially accomplished in clerical script; Ouyang Xun, a friend of his father, held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗謂侍中魏徵曰：「虞世南死後，無人可以論書。

translations.literal: Taizong once said to Palace Attendant Wei Zheng: "After Yu Shinan died, there is no one with whom to discuss books [calligraphy].
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once said to Palace Attendant Wei Zheng: "After Yu Shinan died, there has been no one with whom I can discuss calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 」徵曰：「褚遂良下筆遒勁，甚得王逸少體。

translations.literal: " Zheng said: "Chu Suiliang's brush is forceful and vigorous and very much obtains the style of Wang Yishao.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei replied: "Chu Suiliang's brushwork is forceful and vigorous and captures the manner of Wang Yishao [Wang Xizhi] very well.

sentences.zh: 」太宗即日召令侍書。

translations.literal: " That same day Taizong summoned him and ordered him to attend for writing.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day Taizong summoned him and ordered him to attend the court for calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗出御府金帛購求王羲之書跡，天下爭齎古書詣闕以獻，當時莫能辯其真偽，遂良備論所出，一無舛誤。

translations.literal: Taizong once brought out gold and silk from the imperial treasury to purchase traces of Wang Xizhi's writing; all under Heaven vied to present ancient books to the court, and at the time none could distinguish true from false—Suiliang discussed in full their provenance, without a single error.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once offered gold and silk from the imperial storehouses to buy examples of Wang Xizhi's calligraphy. People everywhere rushed to present old manuscripts to the court, and at the time no one could tell which were genuine. Suiliang discussed the provenance of each piece in detail and never made a mistake.

sentences.zh: 十五年，詔有事太山，先幸洛陽，有星孛於太微，犯郎位。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year an edict ordered rites at Mount Tai; he first visited Luoyang; a comet appeared in Taiwei and encroached on the Chamberlain's seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, an edict ordered ceremonies at Mount Tai. The emperor first visited Luoyang, and a comet appeared in the Taiwei constellation, encroaching on the Chamberlain's seat.

sentences.zh: 遂良言於太宗曰：「陛下撥亂反正，功超前烈，將告成東嶽，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: Suiliang said to Taizong: "Your Majesty has settled disorder and restored the right order; your achievements surpass the former glorious age; you are about to announce completion at the eastern peak—the realm is greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang said to Taizong: "Your Majesty has quelled chaos and restored order, and your achievements surpass those of earlier sage rulers. You are about to complete the rites at the eastern peak, to the great fortune of the realm.

sentences.zh: 而行至洛陽，彗星輒見，此或有所未允合者也。

translations.literal: Yet upon reaching Luoyang the comet promptly appeared—this perhaps indicates something not yet in accord.
translations.idiomatic: Yet upon reaching Luoyang a comet has appeared. This may mean that something is still not in accord with Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 且漢武優柔數年，始行岱禮，臣愚伏願詳擇。

translations.literal: Moreover Emperor Wu of Han hesitated for several years before performing the Dai rites; this subject humbly wishes Your Majesty to choose carefully.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Emperor Wu of Han deliberated for several years before he performed the rites at Mount Tai. I humbly beg Your Majesty to consider the matter with care.

sentences.zh: 」太宗深然之，下詔罷封禪之事。

translations.literal: " Taizong deeply approved and issued an edict halting the feng and shan ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong was deeply persuaded and issued an edict canceling the feng and shan ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 其年，遷諫議大夫，兼知起居事。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Censor and concurrently managed the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was promoted to Censor and concurrently oversaw the imperial diary.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗問：「卿知起居，記錄何事，大抵人君得觀之否？

translations.literal: Taizong once asked: "You oversee the diary—what do you record? May a ruler in general view it?
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once asked: "You oversee the imperial diary. What does it record? As a rule, may a ruler read it?

sentences.zh: 」遂良對曰：「今之起居，古左右史，書人君言事，且記善惡，以為鑑誡，庶幾人主不為非法。

translations.literal: " Suiliang replied: "Today's diary attendants are the ancient left and right scribes; they write the ruler's words and deeds and also record good and evil as a mirror and warning, so that the lord may not act unlawfully.
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang replied: "Today's diary attendants are the ancient left and right scribes. They record the ruler's words and deeds and note good and evil alike, so that they may serve as a mirror and warning and the sovereign may be kept from unlawful conduct.

sentences.zh: 不聞帝王躬自觀史。

translations.literal: One does not hear of emperors and kings personally viewing the history.
translations.idiomatic: I have never heard of an emperor reading the history himself.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「朕有不善，卿必記之耶？

translations.literal: " Taizong said: "If I have something not good, will you surely record it?
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong said: "If I do something wrong, will you record it?

sentences.zh: 」遂良曰：「守道不如守官，臣職當載筆，君舉必記。

translations.literal: " Suiliang said: "Keeping the Way is not as good as keeping one's office; my duty is to bear the brush—the ruler's every act must be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang said: "Upholding the Way is not as binding as upholding one's office. My duty is to hold the brush, and whatever the ruler does must be written down.

sentences.zh: 」黃門侍郎劉洎曰：「設令遂良不記，天下亦記之矣。

translations.literal: " Yellow Gate Attendant Liu Ji said: "Suppose Suiliang did not record it—all under Heaven would still record it.
translations.idiomatic: " Yellow Gate Attendant Liu Ji said: "Even if Suiliang did not write it down, the world would still record it.

sentences.zh: 」太宗以為然。

translations.literal: " Taizong considered this correct.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong agreed that this was so.

sentences.zh: 時魏王為太宗所愛，禮秩如嫡。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Wei was loved by Taizong, and his ritual honors were like those of the legitimate heir.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Wei was a favorite of Taizong, and the ceremonial honors accorded him were like those of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 其年，太宗問侍臣曰：「當今國家何事最急？

translations.literal: That year Taizong asked his attendants: "In the state today, what matter is most urgent?
translations.idiomatic: That year Taizong asked his ministers: "What is the most pressing matter for the state today?

sentences.zh: 」中書侍郎岑文本曰：「《傳》稱『導之以德，齊之以禮』，由斯而言。

translations.literal: " Central Secretariat Attendant Cen Wende said: "The Documents say 'Lead them with virtue, align them with ritual'—from this perspective.
translations.idiomatic: " Central Secretariat Attendant Cen Wende said: "The Analects says, 'Guide them with virtue and align them with ritual.' From that point of view,

sentences.zh: 禮義為急。

translations.literal: Ritual and righteousness are urgent.
translations.idiomatic: ritual and righteousness are what matter most.

sentences.zh: 」遂良進曰：「當今四方仰德，誰敢為非？

translations.literal: " Suiliang advanced and said: "Today the four quarters look up to your virtue—who would dare do wrong?
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang stepped forward and said: "Today the four quarters look up to Your Majesty's virtue. Who would dare act wrongly?

sentences.zh: 但太子、諸王，須有定分，陛下宜為萬代法以遺子孫。

translations.literal: But the crown prince and the various princes must have fixed ranks; Your Majesty should establish a law for ten thousand generations to bequeath to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: But the crown prince and the other princes must each have a fixed place. Your Majesty should set a precedent for ten thousand generations to pass on to your descendants.

sentences.zh: 」太宗曰：「此言是也。

translations.literal: " Taizong said: "These words are correct.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong said: "You are right.

sentences.zh: 朕年將五十，已覺衰怠。

translations.literal: I am nearly fifty and already feel decline and weariness.
translations.idiomatic: I am nearly fifty and already feel my strength failing.

sentences.zh: 既以長子守器東宮，弟及庶子數將五十，心常憂慮，頗在此耳。

translations.literal: Having installed the eldest son Shouqi in the Eastern Palace, my younger brothers and secondary sons number nearly fifty—I constantly worry, and it lies largely in this.
translations.idiomatic: I have already installed my eldest son Shouqi as heir in the Eastern Palace, but my younger sons and sons by concubines number nearly fifty. I worry about this constantly, and that is largely what I mean.

sentences.zh: 但自古嫡庶無良佐，何嘗不傾敗國家？

translations.literal: Yet since antiquity legitimate and secondary lines without good assistants—when have they not overturned and ruined the state?
translations.idiomatic: Yet since antiquity, when legitimate and secondary heirs lack good advisers, has the state not been overturned?

sentences.zh: 公等為朕搜訪賢德，以傅儲宮，爰及諸王，咸求正士。

translations.literal: You all should search out the worthy for me to tutor the heir's palace, and likewise for all the princes seek upright men.
translations.idiomatic: Search out men of talent and virtue to tutor the heir apparent, and for all the princes as well find upright scholars.

sentences.zh: 且事人歲久，即分義情深，非意窺窬，多由此作。

translations.literal: Moreover, when one serves a person for many years, affection and duty grow deep; illicit schemes often arise from this.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when men serve someone for many years, bonds of affection and obligation grow deep, and many illicit ambitions arise from that.

sentences.zh: 」於是限王府官僚不得過四考。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he limited princely household officials to no more than four terms of evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he limited officials in princely households to no more than four terms of service.

sentences.zh: 十七年，太宗問遂良曰：「舜造漆器，禹雕其俎，當時諫舜、禹者十餘人。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Taizong asked Suiliang: "Shun made lacquer vessels and Yu carved his stands; at the time more than ten men remonstrated with Shun and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Taizong asked Suiliang: "Shun had lacquer vessels made, and Yu carved his serving stands. More than ten men remonstrated with Shun and Yu at the time.

sentences.zh: 食器之間，苦諫何也？

translations.literal: Among food vessels, why such earnest remonstrance?
translations.idiomatic: Why such strenuous remonstrance over mere eating utensils?

sentences.zh: 」遂良對曰：「雕琢害農事，纂組傷女工。

translations.literal: " Suiliang replied: "Carving and polishing harm agricultural work; brocade and embroidery harm women's labor.
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang replied: "Carving and polishing harm farming, and brocade work harms women's productive labor.

sentences.zh: 首創奢淫，危亡之漸。

translations.literal: To initiate extravagance and dissipation is the gradual approach of peril and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: To be the first to indulge in luxury is the first step toward ruin.

sentences.zh: 漆器不已，必金為之；

translations.literal: If lacquer vessels do not stop, they must be made of gold;
translations.idiomatic: Once lacquer ware is not enough, vessels must be made of gold;

sentences.zh: 金器不已，必玉為之。

translations.literal: if gold vessels do not stop, they must be made of jade.
translations.idiomatic: and once gold is not enough, they must be made of jade.

sentences.zh: 所以諍臣必諫其漸，及其滿盈，無所復諫。

translations.literal: Therefore remonstrating ministers must remonstrate at the gradual stage; when it is full and overflowing, there is nothing left to remonstrate about.
translations.idiomatic: That is why remonstrating ministers must speak at the first sign of excess, for once luxury is full-blown, nothing more can be said.

sentences.zh: 」太宗以為然，因曰：「夫為人君，不憂萬姓而事奢淫，危亡之機可反掌而待也。

translations.literal: " Taizong considered this correct and said: "For one who is ruler, not to worry about the myriad people but to pursue extravagance—the occasion of peril and ruin may await at a turn of the hand.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong agreed and added: "For a ruler to neglect the people and pursue luxury is to invite ruin in the blink of an eye.

sentences.zh: 」時皇子年幼者多任都督、刺史，遂良上疏曰：「昔兩漢以郡國理人，除郡以外，分立諸子。

translations.literal: " At the time many young princes were appointed area commanders and prefects. Suiliang submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly the two Han dynasties governed the people through commanderies and kingdoms; apart from commanderies they established the various sons separately.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time many young princes were appointed as area commanders and prefects. Suiliang submitted a memorial saying: "In the two Han dynasties the realm was governed through commanderies and kingdoms, and apart from the commanderies the emperor's sons were granted separate domains.

sentences.zh: 割土分疆，雜用周制。

translations.literal: They carved out territory and divided borders, mixing in the Zhou system.
translations.idiomatic: They carved out territory and divided the realm, mixing in elements of the Zhou system.

sentences.zh: 皇唐州縣，祖依秦法。

translations.literal: Our Tang prefectures and counties follow the Qin model in origin.
translations.idiomatic: Our Tang prefectures and counties follow the Qin model.

sentences.zh: 皇子幼年，或授刺史，陛下豈不以王之骨肉，鎮扞四方？

translations.literal: When princes are young they are sometimes given prefectures—is it not that Your Majesty uses the king's own flesh and blood to guard the four quarters?
translations.idiomatic: When princes are still young they are sometimes made prefects. Does Your Majesty not intend your own flesh and blood to guard the four quarters?

sentences.zh: 此之造制，道高前烈。

translations.literal: This institution surpasses the former glorious in principle.
translations.idiomatic: In establishing this system Your Majesty has surpassed the achievements of earlier sage rulers.

sentences.zh: 如臣愚見，有小未盡。

translations.literal: In this subject's foolish view, there is a small matter not yet fully achieved.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, one small point has not yet been fully realized.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: What is it?
translations.idiomatic: What is it?

sentences.zh: 刺史郡帥，民仰以安。

translations.literal: Prefects and commandery leaders—the people look up to them for security.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and commandery chiefs are whom the people rely on for their security.

sentences.zh: 得一善人，部內蘇息；

translations.literal: Obtain one good man and the district revives;
translations.idiomatic: With one good man in office the district revives;

sentences.zh: 遇一不善，合州勞弊。

translations.literal: meet one not good and the whole prefecture is worn and exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: with one bad man the whole prefecture suffers hardship.

sentences.zh: 是以人君愛恤百姓，常為擇賢。

translations.literal: Therefore the ruler who loves and cherishes the hundred surnames constantly selects the worthy for them.
translations.idiomatic: That is why a ruler who cares for the people must always choose the worthy to govern them.

sentences.zh: 或稱河潤九里，京師蒙福；

translations.literal: Some say the river moistens for nine li and the capital receives blessing;
translations.idiomatic: Some say that when a river nourishes the land for nine li, the capital shares in the blessing;

sentences.zh: 或人興歌詠，生為立祠。

translations.literal: or the people rise in song and while he lives a shrine is built for him.
translations.idiomatic: or the people break into song and build shrines to a living official.

sentences.zh: 漢宣帝云：『與我共理者，惟良二千石。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Han said: 'Those who govern with me are only good two-thousand-dan officials.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Han said, 'Those who govern with me are only good prefects.

sentences.zh: 』如臣愚見，陛下兒子內年齒尚幼、未堪臨人者，且留京師，教以經學。

translations.literal: ' In this subject's foolish view, among Your Majesty's sons those still young in years and not yet fit to oversee people should for the present remain in the capital and be taught the classics.
translations.idiomatic: ' In my humble view, among Your Majesty's sons those who are still young and not yet fit to govern should remain in the capital for now and be instructed in the classics.

sentences.zh: 一則畏天之威，不敢犯禁；

translations.literal: First, they will fear Heaven's majesty and not dare violate prohibitions;
translations.idiomatic: First, they will fear Heaven's majesty and not dare break the law;

sentences.zh: 二則觀見朝儀，自然成立。

translations.literal: second, they will observe court ritual and naturally mature.
translations.idiomatic: second, they will observe court ceremony and mature naturally.

sentences.zh: 因此積習，自知為人。

translations.literal: Through accumulated habit they will know themselves as human beings.
translations.idiomatic: Through long habit they will learn how to conduct themselves as men.

sentences.zh: 審堪臨州，然後遣出。

translations.literal: When it is clear they can oversee a prefecture, then send them out.
translations.idiomatic: Only when they are truly fit to govern a prefecture should they be sent out.

sentences.zh: 臣謹按漢明、章、和三帝，能友愛於弟，自茲已降，取為準的。

translations.literal: This subject respectfully notes that the three emperors Ming, Zhang, and He of Han were able to be fraternal toward their younger brothers; from this downward I take them as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully note that Emperors Ming, Zhang, and He of the Han were able to show brotherly love toward their younger brothers. From their example downward I take my standard.

sentences.zh: 封立諸王，雖各有國土，年尚幼小者，召留京師，訓以禮法，垂以恩惠。

translations.literal: They enfeoffed and established the various kings; although each had his own territory, those still young in years were summoned to remain in the capital, instructed in ritual and law, and bestowed with favor.
translations.idiomatic: They enfeoffed their sons as kings, and although each had his own domain, those who were still young were summoned to remain in the capital, instructed in ritual and law, and showered with favor.

sentences.zh: 訖三帝世，諸王數十百人，唯二王稍惡，自余餐和染教，皆為善人。

translations.literal: Through the three emperors' reigns the various kings numbered in the tens and hundreds; only two kings were somewhat bad—the rest, nourished by harmony and steeped in teaching, all became good men.
translations.idiomatic: Through the reigns of those three emperors there were scores of princes, and only two turned out badly. All the rest, nurtured in harmony and steeped in instruction, became good men.

sentences.zh: 則前事已驗，惟陛下詳察。

translations.literal: Thus the former matter has been verified—may Your Majesty examine it in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The precedent has already been proved. I beg Your Majesty to consider it carefully.

sentences.zh: 」太宗深納之。

translations.literal: " Taizong deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong accepted the advice wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 其年，太子承乾以罪廢，魏王泰入侍，太宗面許立為太子。

translations.literal: That year the crown prince Chengqian was deposed for crime; the Prince of Wei Tai entered attendance, and Taizong to his face promised to establish him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: That year Crown Prince Chengqian was deposed for his crimes. The Prince of Wei, Li Tai, attended the emperor in person, and Taizong openly promised to make him crown prince.

sentences.zh: 因謂侍臣曰：「昨青雀自投我懷云：『臣今日始得與陛下為子，更生之日也。

translations.literal: He then said to his attendants: "Yesterday the Green Sparrow threw himself into my arms saying: 'Today I have at last become your son with Your Majesty—it is a day of rebirth.
translations.idiomatic: He then told his ministers: "Yesterday the Green Sparrow [Li Tai] threw himself into my arms and said, 'Today I have at last truly become Your Majesty's son. It is like being born again.

sentences.zh: 臣唯有一子，臣百年之後，當為陛下殺之，傳國晉王。

translations.literal: I have only one son; after my hundred years I will kill him for Your Majesty and pass the state to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: I have only one son. After my hundred years I will kill him for Your Majesty and pass the realm to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 』父子之道，故當天性，我見其如此，甚憐之。

translations.literal: ' The way of father and son should by nature be thus—I saw him like this and greatly pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: ' The bond between father and son ought to be natural. When I saw him speak this way I was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 」遂良進曰：「陛下失言。

translations.literal: " Suiliang advanced and said: "Your Majesty has misspoken.
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang stepped forward and said: "Your Majesty has spoken unwisely.

sentences.zh: 伏願審思，無令錯誤也。

translations.literal: I humbly wish you to consider carefully and not let error stand.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to think this through carefully and not let a mistake stand.

sentences.zh: 安有陛下百年之後，魏王執權為天下之主，而能殺其愛子，傳國於晉王者乎？

translations.literal: How could there be, after Your Majesty's hundred years, the Prince of Wei holding power as lord of all under Heaven yet able to kill his beloved son and pass the state to the Prince of Jin?
translations.idiomatic: How can it be that after Your Majesty's hundred years the Prince of Wei, holding power as ruler of the realm, would kill his own beloved son and pass the state to the Prince of Jin?

sentences.zh: 陛下昔立承乾為太子，而復寵愛魏王，禮數或有逾於承乾者，良由嫡庶不分，所以至此。

translations.literal: Your Majesty formerly established Chengqian as crown prince yet again favored the Prince of Wei, and ceremonial honors sometimes exceeded Chengqian's—truly because legitimate and secondary were not distinguished, it came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty once made Chengqian crown prince, yet you again favored the Prince of Wei, and at times the honors shown him exceeded those of Chengqian. It was because the lines between heir and younger sons were not kept clear that matters came to this pass.

sentences.zh: 殷鑑不遠，足為龜鏡。

translations.literal: The bronze mirror of Yin is not far—sufficient to serve as a tortoise mirror.
translations.idiomatic: The lesson of the recent past is close at hand and should serve as a clear mirror.

sentences.zh: 陛下今日既立魏王，伏願陛下別安置晉王，始得安全耳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty today has already established the Prince of Wei; I humbly wish Your Majesty separately to settle the Prince of Jin—only then will there be security.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty has raised up the Prince of Wei, I beg you to make separate arrangements for the Prince of Jin. Only then will he be safe.

sentences.zh: 」太宗涕泗交下曰：「我不能。

translations.literal: " Taizong, tears and mucus streaming, said: "I cannot.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong wept openly and said, "I cannot.

sentences.zh: 」即日召長孫無忌、房玄齡、李勣與遂良等定策，立晉王為皇太子。

translations.literal: " That same day he summoned Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Li Ji, and Suiliang and others to fix the policy and established the Prince of Jin as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: " That same day he summoned Zhangsun Wuji, Fang Xuanling, Li Ji, Suiliang, and others to settle the succession and installed the Prince of Jin as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時頻有飛雉集於宮殿之內，太宗問群臣曰：「是何祥也？

translations.literal: At the time pheasants frequently flew in and gathered within the palace halls. Taizong asked the assembled ministers: "What omen is this?
translations.idiomatic: At that time wild pheasants kept flying into the palace halls. Taizong asked his ministers: "What omen does this signify?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「昔秦文公時，有童子化為雉，雌者鳴於陳倉，雄者鳴於南陽。

translations.literal: " They replied: "Formerly in the time of Duke Wen of Qin a boy transformed into a pheasant; the female called at Chencang and the male at Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: " They replied: "In the time of Duke Wen of Qin a boy was transformed into a pheasant. The female called at Chencang and the male at Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 童子曰：得雄者王，得雌者霸。

translations.literal: The boy said: he who obtains the male will be king; he who obtains the female will be hegemon.
translations.idiomatic: The boy said, 'He who captures the male will become king; he who captures the female will become hegemon.'

sentences.zh: 文公遂以為寶雞。

translations.literal: Duke Wen thereupon took it as the treasure of Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen thereupon took Chencang as his treasure.

sentences.zh: 後漢光武得雄，遂起南陽而有四海。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Guangwu of Han obtained the male and thereupon rose in Nanyang and possessed the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Guangwu of Han captured the male bird, rose in Nanyang, and won the realm.

sentences.zh: 陛下舊封秦王，故雄雉見於秦地，此所以彰表明德也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty was formerly enfeoffed as Prince of Qin, so the male pheasant appears in Qin territory—this is how your bright virtue is made manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty was once enfeoffed as Prince of Qin, so the male pheasant appears in Qin territory. This is a sign that your bright virtue is being made manifest.

sentences.zh: 」太宗悅曰：「立身之道，不可無學，遂良博識，深可重也。

translations.literal: " Taizong was pleased and said: "The way of establishing oneself cannot be without learning; Suiliang is broadly knowledgeable and deeply to be valued.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong was pleased and said: "The way to stand in the world cannot do without learning. Suiliang is deeply learned and truly worthy of respect.

sentences.zh: 」尋授太子賓客。

translations.literal: " Soon he was appointed Companion to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was appointed Companion to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 時薛延陀遣使請婚，太宗許以女妻之，納其財聘，既而不與。

translations.literal: At the time the Xueyantuo sent envoys to request marriage; Taizong promised a daughter as wife, accepted their bride-price gifts, yet afterward did not give her.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Xueyantuo sent envoys to request a marriage alliance. Taizong promised to give them a princess and accepted their bride-price gifts, but afterward he did not give her.

sentences.zh: 遂良上疏曰：

translations.literal: Suiliang submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 時太宗欲親征高麗，顧謂侍臣曰：「高麗莫離支賊殺其王，虐用其人。

translations.literal: At the time Taizong wished to campaign in person against Goguryeo and, turning to his attendants, said: "Goguryeo's Molizhi treacherously killed his king and cruelly used his people.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Taizong intended to campaign against Goguryeo in person. He turned to his ministers and said: "Molizhi of Goguryeo murdered his king and cruelly oppressed his people.

sentences.zh: 夫出師吊伐，當乘機便，今因其弒虐，誅之甚易。

translations.literal: To send forth the army to console and punish—one should seize the opportune moment; now, taking advantage of his regicide and cruelty, to execute him is very easy.
translations.idiomatic: When one sends an army to console the oppressed and punish the guilty, one must seize the right moment. Now, with this murder and tyranny, it will be very easy to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 」遂良對曰：「陛下兵機神算，人莫能知。

translations.literal: " Suiliang replied: "Your Majesty's military stratagems and divine calculations—no one can know them.
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang replied: "Your Majesty's military stratagems and divine calculations are beyond anyone's ken.

sentences.zh: 昔隋末亂離，手平寇亂。

translations.literal: Formerly at the end of Sui there was chaos and separation; with your own hand you pacified rebellions.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Sui, when the realm was torn apart, you personally quelled the rebellions.

sentences.zh: 及北狄侵邊，西蕃失禮，陛下欲命將擊之，群臣莫不苦諫，陛下獨斷進討，卒並誅夷。

translations.literal: When the northern Di invaded the borders and the western tribes lost ritual propriety, Your Majesty wished to command generals to strike them; the assembled ministers all earnestly remonstrated, yet Your Majesty alone decided to advance and attack, and in the end all were executed and exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: When the northern barbarians raided the frontier and the western tribes showed disrespect, Your Majesty wished to send generals against them. Every minister remonstrated strenuously, yet Your Majesty decided alone to advance, and in the end they were all destroyed.

sentences.zh: 海內之人，徼外之國，畏威懾伏，為此舉也。

translations.literal: People within the seas and states beyond the frontiers feared your majesty and submitted in awe—it was for this action.
translations.idiomatic: The people within the seas and the states beyond the frontiers feared your majesty and submitted. It was because of actions such as these.

sentences.zh: 今陛下將興師遼東，臣意熒惑。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty will raise troops in Liaodong; this subject's mind is confused and doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty intends to raise an army against Liaodong, I am deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 陛下神武，不比前代人君。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is divinely martial, not comparable to rulers of former generations.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is divinely martial and not to be compared with rulers of former ages.

sentences.zh: 兵既渡遼，指期克捷，萬一差跌，無以威示遠方，若再發忿兵，則安危難測。

translations.literal: Once the army has crossed the Liao, victory is expected on schedule; if by any chance there is a slip, there will be no way to display majesty to distant regions—if angry troops are sent forth again, then security and peril cannot be measured.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army crosses the Liao River, victory is expected on schedule. But if by any chance there is a setback, Your Majesty will have no way to display your majesty to distant lands. If you must send angry troops again, the outcome for the state cannot be foreseen.

sentences.zh: 」太宗深然之。

translations.literal: " Taizong deeply approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong strongly agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書李勣曰：「近者延陀犯邊，陛下必欲追擊，此時陛下取魏徵之言，遂失機會。

translations.literal: Minister of War Li Ji said: "Recently the Yantuo violated the borders; Your Majesty surely wished to pursue and strike them. At that time Your Majesty took Wei Zheng's words and thus lost the opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Li Ji said: "When the Yantuo recently raided our borders, Your Majesty surely wanted to pursue them. But at that moment You listened to Wei Zheng and let the opportunity slip away.

sentences.zh: 若如聖策，延陀無一人生還，可五十年間疆場無事。

translations.literal: If according to Your Majesty's sage plan, not one person of the Yantuo would return alive—for fifty years the borders would be without incident.
translations.idiomatic: Had Your Majesty followed your own wise plan, not a single Yantuo raider would have survived, and the frontiers would have been quiet for fifty years.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「誠如卿言，由魏徵誤計耳。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "It is truly as you say—it was because Wei Zheng's plan was mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "You speak truly—it was Wei Zheng's faulty counsel that caused this.

sentences.zh: 朕不欲以一計不當而尤之，後有良算，安肯矢謀。

translations.literal: I do not wish to blame him for one plan being inappropriate; when there are good plans later, how could he refuse to offer counsel?
translations.idiomatic: I do not wish to reproach him for a single poor plan. When he has sound advice in future, why would he refuse to speak?

sentences.zh: 」由是從勣之言，經畫渡遼之師。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he followed Li Ji's words and planned the army to cross the Liao.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he followed Li Ji's advice and set about planning the Liaodong campaign.

sentences.zh: 遂良以太宗銳意三韓，懼其遺悔，翌日上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Suiliang, because Taizong was keenly intent on the Three Han, fearing that he would leave regret, the next day submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Because Taizong was firmly set on campaigns against the Three Han kingdoms, Suiliang feared the emperor would come to regret it and the next day submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 太宗不納。

translations.literal: Taizong did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong did not heed it.

sentences.zh: 十八年，拜黃門侍郎，參綜朝政。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, he was appointed Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and joined in administering court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year of Zhenguan, he was appointed Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and took part in governing the court.

sentences.zh: 高麗莫離支遣使貢白金，遂良言於太宗曰：「莫離支虐弒其主，九夷所不容，陛下以之興兵，將事吊伐，為遼山之人報主辱之恥。

translations.literal: Goguryeo's Molizhi sent envoys to offer tribute of white gold. Suiliang said to Taizong: "Molizhi cruelly murdered his lord, which the nine Yi cannot tolerate. Your Majesty is raising troops against him to console and punish, to avenge for the people of Liao Mountain the shame their lord suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Molizhi of Goguryeo sent envoys bearing tribute of white gold. Suiliang said to Taizong: "Molizhi cruelly murdered his sovereign—something no barbarian people can tolerate. Your Majesty is raising an army to console the oppressed and punish the guilty, to avenge for the people of the eastern mountains the humiliation their lord suffered.

sentences.zh: 古者，討弒君之賊，不受其賂。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when punishing regicides, one did not accept their bribes.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, those who punished regicides did not accept bribes from them.

sentences.zh: 昔宋督遺魯君以郜鼎，桓公受之於太廟，臧哀伯諫曰：『君人者昭德塞違，今滅德立違，而置其賂器於太廟，百官象之，其又何誅焉？

translations.literal: Formerly the Supervisor of Song presented the Duke of Lu with the Bao tripod; Duke Huan received it in the Grand Temple. Zang Aibo remonstrated, saying: 'A ruler should display virtue and block transgression. Now you extinguish virtue and establish transgression, yet place his bribe-vessel in the Grand Temple—the hundred officials will take it as a model—how then can anything be censured?'
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Supervisor of Song presented the Duke of Lu with the Bao tripod, and Duke Huan accepted it in the Grand Temple. Zang Aibo remonstrated, saying: 'A ruler should make virtue manifest and shut out wrongdoing. Now you extinguish virtue and establish wrongdoing, yet place his bribe in the Grand Temple—the officials will take their cue from this—how then can any wrongdoing be punished?'

sentences.zh: 武王克商，遷九鼎於洛邑，義士猶或非之，而況將昭違亂之賂器，置諸太廟，其若之何？

translations.literal: When King Wu conquered Shang and moved the Nine Tripods to the city of Luo, men of principle still sometimes criticized it—how much more if one will display a bribe-vessel of rebellion and disorder and place it in the Grand Temple—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: When King Wu conquered Shang and moved the Nine Tripods to Luoyang, men of principle still criticized the act—how much more objectionable is it to display a bribe associated with rebellion and place it in the Grand Temple? What is one to do?

sentences.zh: 』夫《春秋》之書，百王取法，若受不臣之筐篚，納弒逆之朝貢，不以為愆，何所致伐？

translations.literal: 'The book Spring and Autumn Annals is the model for a hundred kings. If one receives gifts from an insubordinate subject, accepts tribute from a regicide, and does not regard it as fault—what is there to attack him for?'
translations.idiomatic: 'The Spring and Autumn Annals is the standard for kings through the ages. If we accept gifts from a disloyal subject and tribute from a regicide, and do not regard it as wrong—what grounds have we for attacking him?'

sentences.zh: 臣謂莫離支所獻，自不得受。

translations.literal: This subject holds that what Molizhi offers must on no account be accepted.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that what Molizhi offers must not be accepted on any account.

sentences.zh: 」太宗納焉，以其使屬吏。

translations.literal: " Taizong accepted this and handed his envoys over to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizong accepted the advice and turned Molizhi's envoys over to the officials.

sentences.zh: 太宗既滅高昌，每歲調發千餘人防遏其地，遂良上疏曰：

translations.literal: After Taizong had conquered Gaochang, each year more than a thousand men were conscripted to guard that territory. Suiliang submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong conquered Gaochang, more than a thousand men were conscripted each year to garrison the region. Suiliang submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 二十年，太宗於寢殿側別置一院，令太子居，絕不令往東宮。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, Taizong separately established a courtyard beside the sleeping hall and had the crown prince reside there, absolutely not allowing him to go to the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, Taizong had a separate courtyard built beside his bedchamber for the crown prince to live in, and strictly forbade him from going to the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 遂良復上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Suiliang again submitted a memorial remonstrating, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang again submitted a memorial of remonstrance, saying:

sentences.zh: 太宗從之。

translations.literal: Taizong followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 遂良前後諫奏及陳便宜書數十上，多見採納，其年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Suiliang's memorials of remonstrance and petitions setting forth beneficial measures submitted before and after numbered several tens; many were adopted. That year he was additionally granted Silver Blue Light Bulwark Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang submitted dozens of memorials of remonstrance and proposals for practical reforms, many of which were adopted. That year he was additionally promoted to Silver Blue Light Bulwark Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，以本官檢校大理卿，尋丁父憂解。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, with his regular office he was made provisional Grand Minister of Justice; soon after he resigned on mourning for his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was appointed provisional Grand Minister of Justice while retaining his current title. Soon after he resigned to observe mourning for his father's death.

sentences.zh: 明年，起復舊職，俄拜中書令。

translations.literal: The next year he was recalled to his former office; soon he was appointed Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled from mourning to his former post, and soon afterward was appointed Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，太宗寢疾，召遂良及長孫無忌入臥內，謂之曰：「卿等忠烈，簡在朕心。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Taizong fell ill in bed. He summoned Suiliang and Zhangsun Wuji into the inner bedchamber and said to them: "You are loyal and steadfast—I have noted you in my heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, Taizong fell gravely ill. He summoned Suiliang and Zhangsun Wuji to his bedside and said: "You are loyal and steadfast ministers, and I hold you close in my heart.

sentences.zh: 昔漢武寄霍光，劉備托葛亮，朕之後事，一以委卿。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wu of Han entrusted Huo Guang; Liu Bei entrusted Zhuge Liang. My affairs hereafter I wholly entrust to you.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han entrusted Huo Guang, and Liu Bei entrusted Zhuge Liang. I entrust all my remaining affairs entirely to you.

sentences.zh: 太子仁孝，卿之所悉，必須盡誠輔佐，永保宗社。

translations.literal: The crown prince is benevolent and filial—you know this well. You must with full sincerity assist him and forever preserve the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is benevolent and filial, as you well know. You must assist him with your utmost loyalty and preserve the dynasty forever.

sentences.zh: 」又顧謂太子曰：「無忌、遂良在，國家之事，汝無憂矣。

translations.literal: " He also turned and said to the crown prince: "With Wuji and Suiliang here, in matters of the state you need not worry.
translations.idiomatic: " He also turned to the crown prince and said: "With Wuji and Suiliang here, you need not worry about the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 」仍命遂良草詔。

translations.literal: " He still ordered Suiliang to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: " He also ordered Suiliang to draft the imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，賜爵河南縣公。

translations.literal: When Gaozong ascended the throne, he was granted the title Marquis of Henan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, Suiliang was granted the title Marquis of Henan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年，進封郡公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui, he was advanced to Duke of a Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yonghui, he was promoted to Duke of a commandery.

sentences.zh: 尋坐事出為同州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of an offense, he was sent out as Prefect of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, implicated in an offense, he was sent out to serve as Prefect of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，征拜吏部尚書、同中書門下三品，監修國史，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel, Associate of the Third Rank at the Secretariat and Chancellery, Superintendent of the compilation of the National History, and additionally Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was recalled and appointed Minister of Personnel with the concurrent third rank at the Secretariat and Chancellery, put in charge of compiling the national history, and additionally granted the title Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 其月，又兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: That month, he additionally served concurrently as Guest of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he was additionally made Guest of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 四年，代張行成為尚書右僕射，依舊知政事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he replaced Zhang Xingcheng as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, continuing as before to manage state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he replaced Zhang Xingcheng as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and continued to participate in governing as before.

sentences.zh: 六年，高宗將廢皇后王氏，立昭儀武氏為皇后，召太尉長孫無忌、司空李勣、尚書左僕射於志寧及遂良以籌其事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Gaozong was about to depose Empress Wang and establish Lady Wu of Zhao Yi rank as empress. He summoned Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, Minister of Works Li Ji, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Yu Zhining, and Suiliang to plan the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, Gaozong intended to depose Empress Wang and install Lady Wu of the Zhao Yi rank as empress. He summoned Grand Preceptor Zhangsun Wuji, Minister of Works Li Ji, Left Vice Director Yu Zhining, and Suiliang to discuss the matter.

sentences.zh: 將入，遂良謂無忌等曰：「上意欲廢中宮，必議其事，遂良今欲陳諫，眾意如何？

translations.literal: About to enter, Suiliang said to Wuji and the others: "The emperor's intent is to depose the empress of the inner palace; he will surely discuss the matter. Suiliang now wishes to present remonstrance—what is the group's intent?
translations.idiomatic: Before entering, Suiliang said to Wuji and the others: "The emperor means to depose the empress and will surely raise the matter. I intend to remonstrate—what do you all think?

sentences.zh: 」無忌曰：「明公必須極言，無忌請繼焉。

translations.literal: " Wuji said: "Your Excellency must speak to the utmost—I, Wuji, request to follow after.
translations.idiomatic: " Wuji said: "You must speak out forcefully, and I will add my voice after you.

sentences.zh: 」及入，高宗難於發言，再三顧謂無忌曰：「莫大之罪，絕嗣為甚。

translations.literal: " When they entered, Gaozong found it difficult to speak. Repeatedly he turned and said to Wuji: "Of the greatest crimes, having no heir is the gravest.
translations.idiomatic: " When they entered, Gaozong found it hard to broach the subject. Again and again he turned to Wuji and said: "Of great offenses, the worst is to be left without an heir.

sentences.zh: 皇后無胤息，昭儀有子，今欲立為皇后，公等以為何如？

translations.literal: The empress has no offspring; the Lady of Zhao Yi rank has a son. Now I wish to establish her as empress—what do you gentlemen think?
translations.idiomatic: The empress has borne no children, but Lady Wu has a son. I now wish to make her empress—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 」遂良曰：「皇后出自名家，先朝所娶，伏事先帝，無愆婦德。

translations.literal: " Suiliang said: "The empress comes from a distinguished family; the former dynasty chose her in marriage. She served the late emperor—there is no fault in her wifely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang said: "The empress comes from a distinguished house and was chosen in marriage by the previous reign. She served the late emperor faithfully and has committed no fault as a consort.

sentences.zh: 先帝不豫，執陛下手以語臣曰：『我好兒好婦，今將付卿。

translations.literal: When the late emperor was indisposed, he grasped Your Majesty's hand and said to me: 'My good son and good daughter-in-law—I now entrust them to you.'
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor was gravely ill, he took Your Majesty's hand and told me: 'My good son and good daughter-in-law—I now entrust them to your care.'

sentences.zh: 』陛下親承德音，言猶在耳。

translations.literal: ' Your Majesty personally received this imperial charge—the words are still in the ears.
translations.idiomatic: ' Your Majesty received this charge directly from him, and his words still ring in our ears.

sentences.zh: 皇后自此未聞有愆，恐不可廢。

translations.literal: Since then no fault of the empress has been heard—I fear she cannot be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Since then we have heard of no fault on the empress's part—I fear she cannot be deposed.

sentences.zh: 臣今不敢曲從，上違先帝之命，特願再三思審。

translations.literal: This subject now does not dare to follow crookedly in compliance, disobeying the late emperor's command above. I especially wish Your Majesty to reconsider again and again.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not simply go along with this and violate the late emperor's command. I earnestly beg Your Majesty to reconsider again and again.

sentences.zh: 愚臣上忤聖顏，罪合萬死，但願不負先朝厚恩，何顧性命？

translations.literal: This foolish subject above offends the sacred countenance—my crime deserves ten thousand deaths. I only wish not to fail the profound grace of the former dynasty—what care I for life?
translations.idiomatic: I, a foolish minister, offend Your Majesty and deserve death a thousand times over. But I wish only not to betray the deep kindness the previous reign showed me—what care I for my own life?

sentences.zh: 」遂良致笏於殿陛，曰：「還陛下此笏。

translations.literal: " Suiliang placed his tablet on the palace steps and said: "I return to Your Majesty this tablet.
translations.idiomatic: " Suiliang placed his court tablet on the palace steps and said: "I return this tablet to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」仍解巾叩頭流血。

translations.literal: " He still removed his cap and knocked his head until blood flowed.
translations.idiomatic: " He then removed his official cap and knocked his head on the ground until blood flowed.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，令引出。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered him led out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered him removed from the chamber.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌曰：「遂良受先朝顧命，有罪不加刑。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji said: "Suiliang received the former dynasty's deathbed charge—for his offense, do not impose punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji said: "Suiliang was entrusted with the late emperor's final charge—though he has offended, do not punish him.

sentences.zh: 」翌日，帝謂李勣曰：「冊立武昭儀之事，遂良固執不從。

translations.literal: " The next day the emperor said to Li Ji: "Regarding the matter of establishing Lady Wu of Zhao Yi rank as empress, Suiliang stubbornly would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day the emperor said to Li Ji: "On the matter of establishing Lady Wu as empress, Suiliang stubbornly refused to go along.

sentences.zh: 遂良既是受顧命大臣，事若不可，當且止也。

translations.literal: Suiliang, being a minister who received the deathbed charge—if the matter cannot go forward, it should for the time being be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang is a minister entrusted with the late emperor's final charge. If the matter is not feasible, it should be set aside for now.

sentences.zh: 」勣對曰：「此乃陛下家事，不合問外人。

translations.literal: " Ji replied: "This is Your Majesty's family matter—it is not appropriate to ask outsiders.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Ji replied: "This is Your Majesty's private family affair—it is not appropriate to consult outsiders on it.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃立昭儀為皇后，左遷遂良潭州都督。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon established the Lady of Zhao Yi rank as empress and demoted Suiliang to Area Commander of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then installed Lady Wu as empress and demoted Suiliang to Area Commander of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，轉桂州都督。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing, he was transferred to Area Commander of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianqing he was transferred to Area Commander of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又貶為愛州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, he was again demoted to Prefect of Ai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was demoted again to Prefect of Ai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒官，年六十三。

translations.literal: The next year, he died in office at age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died in office at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 遂良卒後二歲餘，許敬宗、李義府奏言長孫無忌所構逆謀，並遂良搧動，乃追削官爵，子孫配流愛州。

translations.literal: More than two years after Suiliang's death, Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu memorialized that Zhangsun Wuji had plotted treason and that Suiliang had abetted and stirred it. His titles and ranks were thereupon posthumously stripped, and his descendants were sentenced to banishment in Ai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than two years after Suiliang's death, Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu charged that Zhangsun Wuji had plotted rebellion and that Suiliang had instigated it. Suiliang's titles were posthumously revoked and his descendants were banished to Ai Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 弘道元年二月，高宗遺詔放還本郡。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Hongdao, Gaozong's testamentary edict released them to return to their native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Hongdao, Gaozong's deathbed edict allowed them to return to their native district.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，則天遺制復遂良及韓瑗爵位。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, Empress Wu Zetian's testamentary instruction restored the ranks of Suiliang and Han Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong, Empress Wu's deathbed edict restored the titles of Suiliang and Han Yuan.

sentences.zh: =韓瑗=

translations.literal: Han Yuan
translations.idiomatic: Han Yuan

sentences.zh: 韓瑗，雍州三原人也。

translations.literal: Han Yuan was a native of Sanyuan in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yuan was a native of Sanyuan in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖紹，隋太僕少卿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shao was Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Han Shao served in the Sui as Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 父仲良，武德初為大理少卿，受詔與郎楚之等掌定律令。

translations.literal: His father Zhongliang, at the beginning of Wude, was Vice Minister of Justice; he received an edict together with Lang Chuzhi and others to oversee the fixing of statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: His father Han Zhongliang served at the beginning of the Wude reign as Vice Minister of Justice and was ordered, together with Lang Chuzhi and others, to supervise the codification of laws and regulations.

sentences.zh: 仲良言於高祖曰：「周代之律，其屬三千，秦法已來，約為五百。

translations.literal: Zhongliang said to Emperor Gaozu: "The laws of the Zhou had three thousand articles; since the Qin code, it has been reduced to about five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongliang said to Emperor Gaozu: "The laws of the Zhou ran to three thousand articles, but since the Qin code the number has been reduced to about five hundred.

sentences.zh: 若遠依周制，繁紊更多。

translations.literal: If one far follows the Zhou system, complexity and confusion would only increase.
translations.idiomatic: If we closely follow the Zhou system, the law will only become more complex and burdensome.

sentences.zh: 且官吏至公，自當奉法，苟若徇己，豈顧刑名？

translations.literal: Moreover, if officials are utterly impartial, they will naturally obey the law; if they indulge themselves, how would they heed punishments and names?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if officials are truly impartial they will naturally obey the law; if they indulge their private interests, what regard will they have for the penal code?

sentences.zh: 請崇寬簡，以允惟新之望。

translations.literal: I request honoring broadness and simplicity to fulfill the hope of renewal.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that we uphold leniency and simplicity, in keeping with the hope for a fresh start.

sentences.zh: 」高祖然之。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Gaozu agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是采定《開皇律》行之，時以為便。

translations.literal: Thereupon they selected and fixed the Kaihuang Code for implementation; at the time it was regarded as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they adopted the Kaihuang Code and put it into effect, and at the time it was considered practical.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，位至刑部尚書、秦州都督府長史、潁川縣公。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan he reached the posts of Minister of Punishments, Senior Administrator of the Qinzhou Area Command headquarters, and Duke of Yingchuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he rose to Minister of Punishments, Senior Administrator of the Qinzhou Area Command, and Duke of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 瑗少有節操，博學有吏才。

translations.literal: Yuan from youth had integrity and moral principle; he was broadly learned and possessed administrative talent.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yuan possessed moral integrity from youth. He was broadly learned and had a talent for administration.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，累至兵部侍郎，襲父潁川公。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan he rose in succession to Vice Minister of War and inherited his father's title Duke of Yingchuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan era he rose to Vice Minister of War and inherited his father's title as Duke of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 永徽三年，拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghui, he was appointed Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yonghui he was appointed Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 四年，與中書侍郎來濟皆同中書門下三品，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he together with Vice Director of the Secretariat Lai Ji were both Associates of the Third Rank at the Secretariat and Chancellery, superintending the compilation of the National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he and Vice Director of the Secretariat Lai Ji were both appointed to the third rank at the Secretariat and Chancellery and put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 五年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was additionally granted Silver Blue Light Bulwark Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was additionally granted the title Silver Blue Light Bulwark Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷侍中，其年兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, he was moved to Palace Attendant; that year he additionally served as Guest of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to Palace Attendant, and that same year additionally served as Guest of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 時高宗欲廢王皇后，瑗涕泣諫曰：「皇后是陛下在籓府時先帝所娶，今無愆過，欲行廢黜，四海之士，誰不惕然？

translations.literal: At the time Gaozong wished to depose Empress Wang. Yuan, weeping, remonstrated, saying: "The empress is one whom the late emperor chose in marriage when Your Majesty was still in the princely establishment. Now there is no fault or offense—if you wish to carry out deposition, which gentleman within the four seas would not be alarmed?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gaozong intended to depose Empress Wang. Han Yuan remonstrated through tears, saying: "The empress was chosen in marriage for Your Majesty by the late emperor when you were still crown prince. She has committed no fault. If you proceed with deposition, what scholar throughout the realm would not be alarmed?

sentences.zh: 且國家屢有廢立，非長久之術。

translations.literal: Moreover, if the state repeatedly has depositions and installations, it is not a long-term policy.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, repeated depositions and installations are no recipe for long-term stability.

sentences.zh: 願陛下為社稷大計，無以臣愚，不垂采察。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty, for the great design of the altars of soil and grain, not because this subject is foolish, to decline to give heed and examination.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty, for the sake of the dynasty's welfare, not to dismiss my foolish words without consideration.

sentences.zh: 」帝不納。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor did not heed him.

sentences.zh: 明日，瑗又諫，悲泣不能自勝。

translations.literal: The next day, Yuan again remonstrated, grieved and weeping beyond self-control.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Han Yuan remonstrated again, weeping with grief he could not contain.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，促令引出。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and urgently ordered him led out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and ordered him removed at once.

sentences.zh: 尋而尚書左僕射褚遂良以忤旨左授潭州都督，瑗復上疏理之曰：

translations.literal: Soon the Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Chu Suiliang, for having defied the imperial intent, was demoted and assigned as Area Commander of Tanzhou. Yuan again submitted a memorial on his behalf, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Soon Left Vice Director Chu Suiliang, for having defied the imperial will, was demoted to Area Commander of Tanzhou. Han Yuan then submitted a memorial in his defense, saying:

sentences.zh: 古之聖王，立諫鼓，設謗木，冀欲聞逆耳之言，甘苦口之議，發揚大化，裨益洪猷，垂令譽於將來，播休聲於不朽者也。

translations.literal: The sage kings of antiquity set up remonstrance drums and erected calumny boards, hoping to hear words that offend the ear and counsel bitter to the mouth, to expand great transformation, benefit vast plans, hang fair renown upon the future, and spread blessed fame upon immortality.
translations.idiomatic: The sage kings of antiquity set up drums for remonstrance and boards for criticism, hoping to hear unwelcome truths and bitter counsel that would extend their great transformation, strengthen their broad designs, win lasting praise for generations to come, and spread a noble reputation through the ages.

sentences.zh: 伏見詔書以褚遂良為潭州都督，臣夙夜思之，用增感激。

translations.literal: I have seen the edict appointing Chu Suiliang Area Commander of Tanzhou; this subject day and night considers it, thereby increasing my stirred feelings.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen the edict appointing Chu Suiliang Area Commander of Tanzhou, and the more I reflect on it day and night, the more deeply I am moved.

sentences.zh: 臣識慚知遠，業謝通經，載撫愚情，誠為未可。

translations.literal: This subject's knowledge is ashamed before those who see far; his craft falls short of mastering the classics. Bearing upon my foolish feelings, it is truly not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: My insight is far less than that of those with foresight, and my learning falls short of mastery of the classics. Yet as I consider the matter in my heart, I feel I cannot remain silent.

sentences.zh: 遂良運偶昇平，道昭前烈，束髮從宦，方淹累稔。

translations.literal: Suiliang's fortune chanced upon rising peace; his Way illuminates former glorious ones. From youth he followed official service—it has just accumulated many years.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang came of age in a time of peace and upholds the principles of the great ministers of old. He entered government service from youth and has served for many years.

sentences.zh: 趨侍陛下，俄歷歲年，不聞涓滴之愆，常睹勤勞之效。

translations.literal: Attending Your Majesty, soon years have passed—not a drop of fault has been heard; constantly the effect of diligent labor has been seen.
translations.idiomatic: He has attended Your Majesty for many years now, and not the slightest fault has ever been reported, while his diligent service has been evident throughout.

sentences.zh: 竭忠誠於早歲，罄直道於茲年。

translations.literal: He exhausted loyalty in early years; he fully expended the straight Way in this year.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his utmost loyalty in his early years and has held fast to integrity until this day.

sentences.zh: 體國忘家，捐身徇物，風霜其操，鐵石其心。

translations.literal: Embodying the state and forgetting the family, casting away the body and following duty—wind and frost his integrity, iron and stone his heart.
translations.idiomatic: He puts the state before his family and gives himself wholly to public service; his integrity is firm as iron and stone.

sentences.zh: 誠可重於皇明，詎專方於曩昔？

translations.literal: Truly he may be valued in the imperial brightness—how could he be specialized only in former times?
translations.idiomatic: Surely he deserves to be valued by this enlightened reign—is his worth to be recognized only in retrospect?

sentences.zh: 且先帝納之於帷幄，寄之以心膂，德逾水石，義冠舟車，公家之利，言無不可。

translations.literal: Moreover, the late emperor received him in the command tent and entrusted him as heart and backbone; his virtue exceeded water and stone, his righteousness crowned chariots and boats—for the public family's benefit, in speech nothing was impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the late emperor welcomed him into his inner counsels and entrusted him as one would his own heart and sinews. His virtue was steadfast as water and stone, his loyalty surpassed all others, and in matters benefiting the state none of his counsel was ever rejected.

sentences.zh: 及纏悲四海，遏密八音，竭忠國家，親承顧托，一德無二，千古懍然。

translations.literal: When grief wrapped the four seas and the eight tones were stilled, he exhausted loyalty for the state and personally received the deathbed entrustment—one virtue without a second, for a thousand ages awe-inspiring.
translations.idiomatic: When grief engulfed the realm and music was stilled at the late emperor's death, he gave his utmost loyalty to the state and personally received the deathbed charge—his single-minded devotion was beyond compare and inspires awe through the ages.

sentences.zh: 此不待臣言，陛下備知之矣。

translations.literal: This needs not await this subject's words—Your Majesty is fully aware of it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty knows all this better than I need to say.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗有此心，未敢聞奏。

translations.literal: This subject has often had this thought but has not dared to report it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: I have long felt this way but have not dared to bring it before the throne.

sentences.zh: 且萬姓失業，旰食忘勞；

translations.literal: Moreover, the myriad people have lost their livelihoods; you eat late and forget fatigue;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the common people are suffering hardship, and Your Majesty rises early and sleeps late in your devotion to governance;

sentences.zh: 一物不安，納隍軫慮，在於微細，寧得過差。

translations.literal: If one thing is not secure, you take concern to heart as if falling into a ditch—with matters in minute detail, how could there be excess error?
translations.idiomatic: When the slightest thing goes wrong you take it to heart as if the realm were in peril—in such careful attention to detail, how could there be any mistake?

sentences.zh: 況社稷之舊臣，陛下之賢佐，無聞罪狀，斥去朝廷，內外氓黎，咸嗟舉措。

translations.literal: How much more so—an old minister of the altars of state, Your Majesty's worthy assistant—no offense heard, yet expelled from the court; within and without, the common people all sigh at the action.
translations.idiomatic: How much more so when a longtime minister of the dynasty, one of Your Majesty's ablest advisors, is dismissed from court without any known offense—people everywhere, within the palace and without, lament this decision.

sentences.zh: 觀其近日言事，披誠懇切，詎肯後陛下之德，異於堯、舜；

translations.literal: Observing his recent words on affairs, he has spread sincerity earnestly—how could he hold back Your Majesty's virtue and make it differ from Yao and Shun?
translations.idiomatic: Judging by his recent memorials, he spoke with the utmost sincerity and candor—surely he wished only to ensure that Your Majesty's virtue would not fall short of that of Yao and Shun;

sentences.zh: 懼陛下之過，塵於史冊。

translations.literal: He feared Your Majesty's fault would be dusted upon the historical records.
translations.idiomatic: He feared only that Your Majesty's errors might be recorded for posterity.

sentences.zh: 而乃深遭厚謗，重負丑言，可以痛志士之心，損陛下之明也。

translations.literal: Yet he has deeply suffered heavy slander and bears repeated shameful words—this can pain the heart of men of resolve and diminish Your Majesty's clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he has been deeply slandered and burdened with shameful accusations. This wounds the hearts of loyal men and dims Your Majesty's discernment.

sentences.zh: 臣聞晉武弘裕，不貽劉毅之誅；

translations.literal: This subject has heard that Emperor Wu of Jin was magnanimous and did not visit punishment on Liu Yi;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Emperor Wu of Jin was magnanimous and did not punish Liu Yi;

sentences.zh: 漢祖深仁，無恚周昌之直。

translations.literal: the Han founder was deeply humane and bore no resentment toward Zhou Chang's bluntness.
translations.idiomatic: and the founder of Han was deeply humane and bore no resentment toward Zhou Chang's blunt honesty.

sentences.zh: 而遂良被遷，已經寒暑，違忤陛下，其罰塞焉。

translations.literal: Yet Suiliang has been transferred and has already passed through cold and heat; in opposing Your Majesty his punishment is sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang has been exiled for more than a year. In opposing Your Majesty he has already suffered punishment enough.

sentences.zh: 伏願纟面鑑無辜，稍寬非罪，俯矜微款，以順人情。

translations.literal: I humbly wish you to look down with compassion on the innocent, slightly ease the undeserved guilt, bend to cherish this slight sincerity, and accord with human feeling.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg Your Majesty to look with compassion on an innocent man, ease his undeserved punishment, and show a little mercy in accord with what the people expect.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝謂瑗曰：「遂良之情，朕亦知之矣。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor said to Yuan: "Suiliang's feelings—I also know them.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, the emperor said to Han Yuan: "I know Suiliang's feelings as well.

sentences.zh: 然其悖戾犯上，以此責之，朕豈有過，卿言何若是之深也！

translations.literal: Yet he was perverse and rebellious, offending his superiors—for this he is blamed. How could I be at fault? Why are your words so extreme!
translations.idiomatic: But he was defiant and insulted his sovereign. For that he is being punished. How can I be at fault? Why do you speak so strongly!

sentences.zh: 」瑗對曰：「遂良可謂社稷忠臣，臣恐以諛佞之輩，蒼蠅點白，損陷忠貞。

translations.literal: " Yuan replied: "Suiliang may be called a loyal minister of the altars of soil and grain. I fear that flatterers and sycophants, like flies spotting white, will harm and entrap the loyal and true.
translations.idiomatic: " Han Yuan replied: "Suiliang may truly be called a loyal minister of the state. I fear that flatterers, like flies spotting a speck on white jade, will slander and destroy a faithful man.

sentences.zh: 昔微子去之而殷國以亡，張華不死而綱紀不亂，國之慾謝，善人其衰。

translations.literal: Formerly when Weizi left, the state of Yin perished; when Zhang Hua did not die, the statutes were not disordered. When a state is about to decline, good men are the first to wane.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when Weizi left, the Yin state perished; when Zhang Hua lived, the laws were not thrown into chaos. When a state is about to fall, good men are the first to decline.

sentences.zh: 今陛下富有四海，八紘清泰，忽驅逐舊臣，而不垂省察乎！

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty possesses the four seas and the eight directions are clear and tranquil—suddenly to drive out an old minister and not bend to examine and consider!
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty possesses all within the four seas and the realm is at peace. Will you suddenly drive out an old minister and not look into the matter carefully!

sentences.zh: 伏願違彼覆車，以收往過，垂勸誡於事君，則群生幸甚。

translations.literal: I humbly wish you to avoid that overturned cart, recover past errors, bestow admonition on serving one's lord—then the multitude will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to avoid repeating past mistakes, recall your former minister, and show by your example how a ruler should heed loyal counsel. Then the people will be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 」帝竟不納。

translations.literal: " The emperor in the end did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not be persuaded.

sentences.zh: 瑗以言不見用，憂憤上表，請歸田裡，詔不許。

translations.literal: Yuan, because his words were not employed, in grief and anger submitted a memorial requesting to return to his fields and villages; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Because his advice went unheeded, Han Yuan submitted a memorial in grief and anger asking to retire to his home estate, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，許敬宗、李義府希皇后之旨，誣奏瑗與褚遂良潛謀不軌，以桂州用武之地，故授遂良桂州刺史，實以為外援。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianqing, Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu, courting the empress's intent, falsely memorialized that Yuan and Chu Suiliang secretly plotted sedition; because Guizhou was a place for deploying military force, they had appointed Suiliang Guizhou prefect—in reality as external support.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianqing, Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu, acting on the empress's wishes, falsely accused Han Yuan and Chu Suiliang of plotting rebellion. They claimed that because Guizhou was a strategic military region, Suiliang had been made prefect of Guizhou to serve as outside support for the plot.

sentences.zh: 於是更貶遂良為愛州刺史，左授瑗振州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Suiliang was further demoted to Ai Prefecture prefect and Yuan was transferred left to Zhen Prefecture prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Suiliang was further demoted to prefect of Ai Prefecture, and Han Yuan was transferred to prefect of Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 四年，卒官，年五十四。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he died in office, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he died in office at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 明年，長孫無忌死，敬宗等又奏瑗與無忌通謀，遣使殺之。

translations.literal: The next year Zhangsun Wuji died; Jingzong and others again memorialized that Yuan had conspired with Wuji and sent envoys to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Zhangsun Wuji died. Jingzong and others then accused Han Yuan of conspiring with Wuji and sent agents to kill him.

sentences.zh: 及使至，瑗已死，更發棺驗屍而還，籍沒其家，孫配徙嶺表。

translations.literal: When the envoys arrived Yuan was already dead; they further opened the coffin and examined the corpse before returning, registered and confiscated his household, and his grandsons were banished to the region beyond the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys arrived Han Yuan was already dead. They opened his coffin to verify the corpse, then returned. His property was confiscated and his grandsons were exiled to the far south.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，則天遺制令復其官爵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong, Wu Zetian's final testament ordered restoration of his offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shenlong, Empress Wu's final testament ordered that his offices and titles be restored.

sentences.zh: =來濟=

translations.literal: Lai Ji
translations.idiomatic: Lai Ji

sentences.zh: 來濟，揚州江都人，隋左翊衛大將軍榮國公護子也。

translations.literal: Lai Ji was a man of Jiangdu in Yangzhou, son of Hu, Duke of Rong of the Sui, General of the Left Wing Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Ji was from Jiangdu in Yangzhou, the son of Hu, Duke of Rong, who had served the Sui as General of the Left Wing Guard.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之難，闔門遇害。

translations.literal: In the disaster of Yuwen Huaji, the entire household suffered harm.
translations.idiomatic: During the catastrophe wrought by Yuwen Huaji, his entire family was killed.

sentences.zh: 濟幼逢家難，流離艱險，而篤志好學，有文詞，善談論，尤曉時務。

translations.literal: Ji in youth encountered family disaster, wandered through hardship and peril, yet was devoted in will and loved learning; he had literary compositions, was skilled in discourse, and especially understood current affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ji suffered family disaster in his youth and wandered through hardship, yet he devoted himself to study. He was accomplished in letters, skilled in debate, and especially well versed in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，貞觀中累轉通事舍人。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and in Zhenguan was repeatedly transferred to Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and during Zhenguan rose through several posts to Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾之敗，太宗謂侍臣曰：「欲何以處承乾？

translations.literal: When the crown prince Chengqian failed, Taizong said to his attendants: "How do you wish to deal with Chengqian?
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Chengqian's downfall, Taizong asked his ministers: "How should Chengqian be dealt with?

sentences.zh: 」群臣莫敢對，濟進曰：「陛下上不失作慈父，下得盡天年，即為善矣。

translations.literal: " The assembled ministers dared not reply. Ji advanced and said: "Your Majesty above will not fail as a loving father; below he may complete his natural years—that is good enough.
translations.idiomatic: " No minister dared answer. Ji stepped forward and said: "Your Majesty will not fail as a loving father, and the prince may live out his natural span. That is enough.

sentences.zh: 」帝納其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 俄除考功員外郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十八年，初置太子司議郎，妙選人望，遂以濟為之，仍兼崇賢館直學士。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the crown prince's Master of Discussion was first established; men of outstanding reputation were finely selected, and Ji was appointed to it, while still concurrently serving as Academician in the Palace of Exalted Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year the office of Master of Discussion for the crown prince was first created. Men of outstanding reputation were sought, and Ji was appointed, while also serving as Academician in the Palace of Exalted Virtue.

sentences.zh: 尋遷中書舍人，與令狐德棻等撰《晉書》。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Secretariat Drafter and with Linghu Defen and others compiled the Book of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Secretariat Drafter and joined Linghu Defen and others in compiling the Book of Jin.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，拜中書侍郎，兼弘文館學士，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui he was appointed Central Secretariat Attendant, concurrently Academician of the Hongwen Hall, supervising compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonghui he was appointed Central Secretariat Attendant, concurrently served as Academician of the Hongwen Hall, and supervised compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 四年，同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he became Third Grade at the Central Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made Third Grade at the Central Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 五年，加銀青光祿大夫，以修國史功封南陽縣男，賜物七百段。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was given Silver Blue Light Bulwark Grand Master; for merit in compiling the national history he was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanyang and granted seven hundred rolls of goods.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to Silver Blue Light Bulwark Grand Master. For his work on the national history he was enfeoffed as Baron of Nanyang and granted seven hundred rolls of goods.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷中書令、檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Grand Secretary and Acting Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Grand Secretary and Acting Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 時高宗欲立昭儀武氏為宸妃，濟密表諫曰：「宸妃古無此號，事將不可。

translations.literal: At the time Gaozong wished to establish the Brilliant Consort Lady Wu as Chen Consort. Ji submitted a secret memorial remonstrating: "Chen Consort—anciently there was no such title; the matter cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gaozong wished to create the Brilliant Consort Lady Wu as Chen Consort. Ji submitted a secret memorial of remonstrance: "There was never such a title as Chen Consort in antiquity. The matter cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 」武皇后既立，濟等懼不自安；

translations.literal: " After Empress Wu was established, Ji and others feared they could not be at ease;
translations.idiomatic: " After Empress Wu was established, Ji and his allies lived in fear;

sentences.zh: 後乃抗表稱濟忠公，請加賞慰，而心實惡之。

translations.literal: later she submitted a forthright memorial praising Ji as loyal and fair, requesting added reward and consolation, yet in heart truly hated him.
translations.idiomatic: yet she later submitted a memorial praising Ji as loyal and upright and asking that he be rewarded, while in her heart she truly hated him.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，兼太子賓客，進爵為侯，中書令如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing he was concurrently Companion to the Crown Prince, advanced in rank to Marquis, Grand Secretary as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianqing he was additionally appointed Companion to the Crown Prince and advanced to Marquis, while retaining his post as Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 二年，又兼太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the second year he was again concurrently Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household.
