translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was additionally made Steward of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 尋而許敬宗等奏濟與褚遂良朋黨構扇，左授台州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon Xu Jingzong and others memorialized that Ji had formed a faction with Chu Suiliang and incited trouble; he was transferred left to Taizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xu Jingzong and others accused Ji of forming a faction with Chu Suiliang and stirring up trouble. He was transferred to prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，徙庭州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was moved to Ting Prefecture prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was transferred to prefect of Ting Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，突厥入寇，濟總兵拒之，謂其眾曰：「吾嘗掛刑網，蒙赦性命，當以身塞責，特報國恩。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo the Turks invaded; Ji commanded troops to resist them and said to his host: "I once hung in the criminal net and received pardon of life—I should use my body to fill the obligation and repay the state's grace in particular.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longshuo the Turks invaded. Ji took command of the army to resist them and told his troops: "I once faced execution and was spared. I should repay the state's grace with my life.

sentences.zh: 」遂不釋甲冑赴賊，沒於陣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon without removing armor he went toward the enemy and perished in the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: " He did not remove his armor and charged the enemy, dying in battle.

sentences.zh: 時年五十三，贈楚州刺史，給靈輿遞還鄉。

translations.literal: He was then fifty-three; posthumously he was given Chu Prefecture prefect and a funeral carriage was provided to escort him home.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-three years old. He was posthumously appointed prefect of Chu Prefecture, and a funeral carriage was provided to return his body home.

sentences.zh: 有文集三十捲，行於代。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in thirty scrolls, circulating in his generation.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in thirty scrolls, which circulated in his day.

sentences.zh: 兄 亙濟兄亙，有學行，與濟齊名。

translations.literal: Elder brother Heng—Ji's elder brother Heng had learning and conduct and was as famous as Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Heng was a man of learning and integrity and was as renowned as Ji.

sentences.zh: 上元中，官至黃門侍郎、同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: In Shangyuan he reached the post of Yellow Gate Attendant and Third Grade at the Central Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shangyuan reign he rose to Yellow Gate Attendant and Third Grade at the Central Secretariat and Chancellery.

sentences.zh: =上官儀=

translations.literal: Shangguan Yi
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Yi

sentences.zh: 上官儀，本陝州陝人也。

translations.literal: Shangguan Yi was originally a man of Shan in Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Yi was originally from Shan in Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父弘，隋江都宮副監，因家於江都。

translations.literal: His father Hong was Sui Deputy Supervisor of the Jiangdu Palace and thereby made his home in Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hong had served the Sui as Deputy Supervisor of the Jiangdu Palace and settled the family in Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 大業末，弘為將軍陳稜所殺，儀時幼，藏匿獲免。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye, Hong was killed by the general Chen Suo; Yi was then young and by hiding escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye reign Hong was killed by the general Chen Suo. Yi was still a child and survived by hiding.

sentences.zh: 因私度為沙門，游情釋典，尤精《三論》，兼涉獵經史，善屬文。

translations.literal: Thereupon he privately crossed over to become a monk, wandered in affection through Buddhist scriptures, was especially expert in the Three Treatises, and also ranged through the classics and histories, skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He then secretly became a monk, devoted himself to Buddhist scriptures, and became especially expert in the Three Treatises. He also read widely in the classics and histories and was skilled at writing.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，楊仁恭為都督，深禮待之。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan Yang Rengong was area commander and treated him with deep ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan, when Yang Rengong was area commander, he treated Yi with great respect.

sentences.zh: 舉進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞其名，召授弘文館直學士。

translations.literal: Taizong heard his name and summoned him to appoint him Academician in the Hongwen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong heard of him and summoned him to serve as Academician in the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 累遷秘書郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 時太宗雅好屬文，每遣儀視草，又多令繼和，凡有宴集，儀嘗預焉。

translations.literal: At the time Taizong elegantly loved literary composition; he often sent Yi to review drafts and also frequently ordered him to continue and harmonize. Whenever there were banquets and gatherings, Yi was often among them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong loved literature and often had Yi review his drafts and compose matching pieces. Yi was a regular presence at court banquets.

sentences.zh: 俄又預撰《晉書》成，轉起居郎，加級賜帛。

translations.literal: Soon he again participated in compiling the Book of Jin to completion, was transferred to Attendant of the Imperial Diary, and was given an added grade and silk.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took part in completing the Book of Jin, was transferred to Attendant of the Imperial Diary, and received an additional rank and a gift of silk.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，遷秘書少監。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, he was transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, Yi was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，加銀青光祿大夫、西台侍郎、同東西台三品，兼弘文館學士如故。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo he was given Silver Blue Light Bulwark Grand Master, Western Terrace Attendant, Third Grade at the Eastern and Western Terraces, concurrently Academician of the Hongwen Hall as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Longshuo he was made Silver Blue Light Bulwark Grand Master, Western Terrace Attendant, and Third Grade at the Eastern and Western Terraces, while retaining his post as Academician of the Hongwen Hall.

sentences.zh: 本以詞彩自達，工於五言詩，好以綺錯婉媚為本。

translations.literal: Originally he distinguished himself through literary color, was skilled in five-character poetry, and liked to take brocade-like intricacy and graceful charm as his foundation.
translations.idiomatic: He had risen through the brilliance of his writing and was skilled in five-character verse, favoring an ornate and graceful style.

sentences.zh: 儀既貴顯，故當時多有效其體者，時人謂為上官體。

translations.literal: Once Yi was noble and prominent, many at the time imitated his style; people of the time called it the Shangguan style.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yi had risen to high rank, many poets of the day imitated his manner, which came to be known as the Shangguan style.

sentences.zh: 儀頗恃才任勢，故為當代所嫉。

translations.literal: Yi rather relied on talent and wielded power, and therefore was envied by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Yi relied heavily on his talent and power, and for that reason was resented by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 麟德元年，宦者王伏勝與梁王忠抵罪，許敬宗乃構儀與忠通謀，遂下獄而死，家口籍沒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Linde the eunuch Wang Fusheng and the Prince of Liang Zhong were found guilty; Xu Jingzong then framed Yi as having conspired with Zhong, and he was cast into prison and died; his household was registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Linde the eunuch Wang Fusheng and Prince Zhong of Liang were found guilty of crimes. Xu Jingzong then framed Yi as having conspired with Zhong. Yi was imprisoned and died, and his household was confiscated.

sentences.zh: 子庭芝，歷位周王府屬。

translations.literal: His son Tingzhi held posts as an official of the Prince of Zhou's household.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tingzhi had served as an official in the household of the Prince of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 與儀俱被殺。

translations.literal: He was killed together with Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed together with Yi.

sentences.zh: 庭芝有女，中宗時為昭容，每侍帝草制誥，以故追贈儀為中書令、秦州都督、楚國公；

translations.literal: Tingzhi had a daughter who in Zhongzong's time was Brilliant Lady; she often attended the emperor in drafting edicts and proclamations—for this reason Yi was posthumously given Grand Secretary, Qinzhou Area Commander, and Duke of Chu;
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhi had a daughter who under Zhongzong served as Brilliant Lady and often helped the emperor draft edicts. For this reason Yi was posthumously appointed Grand Secretary, Area Commander of Qinzhou, and Duke of Chu;

sentences.zh: 庭芝黃門侍郎、岐州刺史、天水郡公，仍令以禮改葬。

translations.literal: Tingzhi was given Yellow Gate Attendant, Qi Prefecture prefect, and Duke of Tianshui, and they were still ordered to be reburied according to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: and Tingzhi was posthumously made Yellow Gate Attendant, prefect of Qi Prefecture, and Duke of Tianshui. They were reburied with full ceremony.

sentences.zh: =史臣曰=

translations.literal: The historiographer says:
translations.idiomatic: The Historiographer's Comment

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：褚河南上書言事，亹癖有經世遠略。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Chu of Henan submitted memorials on affairs—diligent and principled, with far-reaching plans to order the age.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Chu Suiliang of Henan submitted memorials on affairs of state with tireless integrity and far-reaching vision for ordering the realm.

sentences.zh: 魏徵、王珪之後，骨鯁風彩，落落負王佐器者，殆難其人。

translations.literal: After Wei Zheng and Wang Gui, in bone and spine and wind and color, openly bearing the vessels of a king's assistant—one may hardly find his equal.
translations.idiomatic: After Wei Zheng and Wang Gui, among men of stern integrity and commanding presence who openly bore the capacity of a chief minister, his equal was hard to find.

sentences.zh: 名臣事業，河南有焉。

translations.literal: Among famous ministers' achievements, Henan had his share.
translations.idiomatic: Among the achievements of famous ministers, Henan had his place.

sentences.zh: 昔齊人饋樂而仲尼去，戎王溺妓而由余奔，婦人之言，聖哲懼罹其禍，況二佞據衡軸之地，為正人之魑魅乎！

translations.literal: Formerly when the men of Qi presented music Confucius departed; when the Rong king drowned in entertainers Youyu fled—a woman's words, and sages and wise men feared to suffer their calamity—how much more when two flatterers occupied the pivot of the balance beam and became the evil spirits of upright men!
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Confucius left Qi when music was offered to him, and Youyu fled when the Rong king drowned himself in entertainers. Even sages feared the harm that could come from a woman's words. How much worse when two flatterers held the pivot of power and became demons haunting upright men!

sentences.zh: 古之志士仁人，一言相期，死不之悔，況於君臣之間，受託孤之寄，而以利害禍福，忘平生之言哉！

translations.literal: Ancient men of resolve and humane men, with one word pledged to each other, did not regret unto death—how much more between ruler and minister, receiving the charge of a lone orphan, to forget words of a lifetime for profit, harm, disaster, and fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Men of resolve in antiquity, once they pledged themselves with a single word, did not regret it even unto death. How much more between ruler and minister, when one has received the charge of a dying sovereign, to forget one's lifelong pledge for the sake of profit, loss, or personal safety!

sentences.zh: 而韓、來諸公，可謂守死善道，求福不回者焉。

translations.literal: Yet the gentlemen Han, Lai, and the rest may be called those who kept death and upheld the good Way, seeking fortune without turning back.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yuan, Lai Ji, and their fellows may truly be called men who upheld the Way unto death and would not turn aside even to seek their own fortune.

translations.literal: Eulogy:
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy

sentences.zh: 贊曰：褚公之言，和樂愔愔，鐘石在虡，動成雅音。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Lord Chu's words were harmonious and joyful, gentle and serene; bell and stone on the stand—when moved they formed elegant sound.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: Lord Chu's words were harmonious and serene, like bells and chimes on their stand—when struck they formed music of the highest refinement.

sentences.zh: 二猘雙吠，三賢一心。

translations.literal: Two mad dogs barked in pairs; three worthies were of one heart.
translations.idiomatic: Two mad dogs barked together; three worthy men stood as one.

sentences.zh: 人皆觀望，我不浮沉。

translations.literal: Others all watched and waited; I did not drift with the current.
translations.idiomatic: While others watched and waited, they would not drift with the tide.
